Check an arm for drift against a frozen benchmark

Source: R/core-bench-drift.R
hr_drift_check.Rd

Reruns arm live on the items of a frozen hr_benchmark() and compares the live runs with the frozen ones item by item. The live rerun is itself an hr_benchmark() of the arm, with the frozen benchmark's split and fresh draws, and is returned in $live; it can be reported with hr_report() or kept as the next frozen sample.

Usage

hr_drift_check(
  frozen,
  arm,
  runs = 5,
  alpha = 0.05,
  alert = NULL,
  client,
  reference,
  scorer = hr_scorer_exact(),
  governor = NULL,
  B = 2000,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'hr_drift_check'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

Arguments

frozen

An hr_bench from hr_benchmark() holding at least 5 runs of arm: the frozen sample.

arm

The hr_arm() to rerun, the same arm (by hash) that the frozen benchmark ran.

runs

The number of live runs, a whole number, at least 2, so that the live runs have replicate flips of their own. As many as the frozen runs compares like with like.

alpha

The level of each test, in (0, 0.5): two-sided for (a), one-sided for (b).

alert

The accuracy change that must not go unnoticed, a proportion in (0, 1), or NULL for no alert.

client

The client the live runs call; see hr_benchmark().

reference

The hr_reference() the frozen benchmark scored.

scorer

The scorer the frozen benchmark used; checked by name.

governor

An hr_governor() the live rerun is held to, or NULL to take the limits from gr_options().

B

The number of cluster resamples, at least 100.

seed

The seed of the live runs' private random stream and of the resamples. NULL takes the frozen benchmark's seed plus 1, so an arm that samples makes fresh draws rather than replaying the frozen ones.

x

An hr_drift_check.

digits

Digits to print.

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class hr_drift_check, a list with

arm, arm_hash, reference_hash, frozen_runs, live_runs, n_items, n_clusters, alpha, alert, B, seed

What was compared and how.

items

One row per labelled item: cluster, item, frozen_accuracy (p_i), live_accuracy (q_i), change ("lost" when most frozen runs were right and most live runs wrong, "gained" the reverse, "worse" or "better" for a smaller move, "same" when p_i = q_i), frozen_outcome and live_outcome (the most common scored output, or the failure kind in angle brackets), and replicate_flip (f_i), live_flip (h_i), cross_flip (g_i) and excess (e_i). change compares shares of runs only: on an item whose frozen or live runs disagree among themselves (replicate_flip or live_flip above 0), a move can be ordinary run-to-run variation, and only test (b) says whether the moves as a whole exceed it. An item that was stable before (replicate_flip 0) and moved is a real flip.

accuracy

Test (a): frozen, live, change, lower, upper, bca (FALSE when the percentile interval stood in), p_value, detected.

mcnemar

The cross-check: statistic, df, p_value, detected, and agrees, whether it reaches the same decision as test (a).

instability

Test (b): replicate_flip, live_flip, cross_flip, excess, lower (the one-sided bound), bca, p_value, detected.

replicate_pairs, cross_pairs

The flip rate over items of each pair of frozen runs, and of each frozen run with each live run.

drift

Whether either test rejected.

alert_crossed

Whether the interval of test (a) lies wholly beyond the alert, a change at least that large; NA without alert or without an interval.

alert_not_ruled_out

Whether the interval of test (a) reaches beyond the alert, so a change that large cannot be ruled out; NA as for alert_crossed.

live

The live hr_bench.

notes

What the reader should know about the result.

Details

Two tests are run, with alpha and alert fixed in the call before anything is rerun, so neither can be chosen after the result is seen.

(a) Accuracy change. For item i, p_i is the share of the frozen runs that were correct and q_i the share of the live runs. The change is mean(q_i - p_i) over items, live minus frozen. Its two-sided interval at level 1 - alpha is a BCa cluster bootstrap (Efron 1987): each of the B resamples draws whole clusters with replacement, with all their items and runs, so the frozen and live values of an item stay paired. Accuracy changed when the interval excludes 0.

As a cross-check the clustered McNemar test of Obuchowski (1998) is run on the same item accuracies. With x_1k and x_2k the sums of p_i and q_i over the items of cluster k, n_k its items, N the items and K the clusters, the estimates are P_j = sum_k x_jk / N and

X^2 = (P_1 - P_2)^2 / (V_1 + V_2 - 2 V_12),

V_j = K / ((K - 1) N^2) sum_k (x_jk - n_k P_j)^2, V_12 = K / ((K - 1) N^2) sum_k (x_1k - n_k P_1) (x_2k - n_k P_2),

referred to a chi-squared distribution on 1 degree of freedom. An unclustered McNemar test is not offered: it treats items from one document as independent and overstates the evidence.

(b) Excess instability. A model that answers differently from run to run flips items between any two runs, frozen or live. So the flips between frozen and live runs are compared with the flips among replicate runs. With R_f frozen runs of which k_i were correct on item i, and R_l live runs of which m_i were,

f_i = 2 k_i (R_f - k_i) / (R_f (R_f - 1))

is the share of pairs of frozen runs that disagree on item i,

h_i = 2 m_i (R_l - m_i) / (R_l (R_l - 1))

the same share among the live runs, and

g_i = (k_i (R_l - m_i) + (R_f - k_i) m_i) / (R_f R_l)

the share of frozen-live pairs that disagree. With frozen accuracy p and live accuracy q on the item, f_i, h_i and g_i estimate 2 p (1 - p), 2 q (1 - q) and p (1 - q) + q (1 - p) without bias, so the item's excess

e_i = g_i - (f_i + h_i) / 2

estimates (p - q)^2. It is 0 in expectation when nothing changed and above 0 for any move, in either direction and from any starting accuracy, so it sees losses and gains that cancel in the accuracy change and noisy items that turn deterministic. The live replicate flips h_i enter beside the frozen ones because g_i - f_i alone estimates (q - p) (1 - 2 p), which is 0 for an item at p = 0.5 whatever q is and below 0 when an item settles toward 0 or 1. The test is one-sided: instability is in excess when the lower BCa bound of mean(e_i) at one-sided level alpha, from the same cluster resamples, is above 0. The flip rate of every pair of frozen runs and of every frozen-live pair is returned too, so the frozen replicate distribution can be read directly.

P-values of the bootstrap tests are the smallest level at which the test rejects, found by bisection over [1 / (B + 1), 0.5]; 1 when it does not reject even at 0.5.

Drift and alert. drift is TRUE when either test rejects. Each test runs at alpha, so the chance that drift is TRUE with no change at all can reach 2 alpha; pass alpha / 2 to hold it at alpha. alert, when given, is the accuracy change, in points as a proportion, that may not go unnoticed, and it is read two ways. The alert is crossed (alert_crossed) when the whole interval of test (a) lies beyond -alert or alert: a change at least that large is shown. A change of alert is not ruled out (alert_not_ruled_out) when the interval reaches beyond -alert or alert. A small or noisy frozen sample often cannot rule it out even with no change at all, which says the sample cannot vouch for the arm, not that the arm moved. Size the sample with hr_n_needed().

What is refused. Fewer than 5 frozen runs of the arm (class hr_drift_few_runs): with fewer, the replicate flips are too few pairs to compare against. An arm whose hash is not the frozen arm's, a reference or scorer other than the frozen benchmark's (class hr_drift_mismatch): those would compare two configurations, which is hr_report()'s job. A live run any of whose requests a cache or a recording answered (class hr_drift_not_live): that is the frozen reply again, not the model today. Turn cache reads off for the drift check.

The cluster bootstrap can undercover below 300 items or 30 clusters, and the result notes it. With one cluster there is nothing to resample, and both tests are left NA.

References

Efron, B. (1987). Better bootstrap confidence intervals. Journal of the American Statistical Association 82(397), 171-185.

Obuchowski, N. A. (1998). On the comparison of correlated proportions for clustered data. Statistics in Medicine 17(13), 1495-1507.

See also

hr_benchmark(), hr_report(), hr_n_needed()

Examples

ref <- hr_reference(
  items = list(q1 = "France", q2 = "Peru", q3 = "Chad", q4 = "Fiji",
               q5 = "Chile", q6 = "Laos"),
  labels = c("Paris", "Lima", "N'Djamena", "Suva", "Santiago", "Vientiane"),
  cluster = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "c", "c"), split = "test")
capitals <- c(France = "Paris", Peru = "Lima", Chad = "N'Djamena", Fiji = "Suva",
              Chile = "Santiago", Laos = "Vientiane")
answer <- function(capitals) {
  gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) {
    capitals[[sub("Capital of ", "", messages[[1]]$content)]]
  })
}
ask <- hr_arm("ask", function(item, ctx) ctx$call(paste0("Capital of ", item))$text)
frozen <- hr_benchmark(ask, ref, runs = 5, client = answer(capitals))

# Months later the model gets two capitals wrong.
today <- capitals
today[c("Chad", "Laos")] <- c("Ndjamena", "Luang Prabang")
drift <- hr_drift_check(frozen, ask, client = answer(today), reference = ref,
                        alert = 0.1, B = 500)
drift
#> <hr_drift_check> arm 'ask': 5 frozen run(s) vs 5 live, 6 item(s) in 3 cluster(s); alpha 0.05
#> (a) Accuracy: frozen 1.000, live 0.667, change -0.333 [-0.500, -0.167], p 0.0122; changed: yes
#>     Clustered McNemar (Obuchowski): X^2 4.000, p 0.0455; agrees: yes
#> (b) Flips: between frozen runs 0.000, between live runs 0.000, frozen vs live 0.333, excess 0.333 (one-sided lower 0.000), p 0.333; in excess: no
#>     Frozen pairs flip 0.000 to 0.000; frozen-live pairs 0.333 to 0.333
#> Drift: yes; alert at 0.100: crossed
#> Items: lost 2, gained 0, worse 0, better 0, same 4 
#>  item cluster change frozen live  frozen_outcome live_outcome 
#>  q3   b       lost   1.000  0.000 n'djamena      ndjamena     
#>  q6   c       lost   1.000  0.000 vientiane      luang prabang
#> Note: 6 items in 3 clusters fall short of 300 items and 30 clusters, where the cluster bootstrap can undercover; read the tests as approximate. 
drift$items[drift$items$change != "same", ]
#>   cluster item frozen_accuracy live_accuracy change frozen_outcome
#> 3       b   q3               1             0   lost      n'djamena
#> 6       c   q6               1             0   lost      vientiane
#>    live_outcome replicate_flip live_flip cross_flip excess
#> 3      ndjamena              0         0          1      1
#> 6 luang prabang              0         0          1      1
